title: PRD: Soft-pin exemptions and runtime sanity gates for community model onboarding
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem statement: We frequently accept community/open models into the catalog with soft-pinning semantics (allowing runtime to substitute compatible variants). However, ambiguous compatibility metadata and no formal exemption path cause downstream reliability incidents and churn for runtime and infra teams. This PRD defines a lightweight decision surface for when a model may be exempted from soft-pinning (i.e., must be strictly version-pinned), the runtime sanity gates required for safe soft-pin fallback, and the onboarding acceptance criteria that product, runtime, and catalog intake teams must enforce. Goals: 1) Reduce production incidents caused by silent behavioral changes when variants are substituted; 2) Provide clear, testable signals to runtime for safe fallback; 3) Keep onboarding lightweight for low-risk community models; 4) Enable deterministic rollback when a compatibility regression is detected. Non-goals: Redesigning the entire model catalog schema or introducing heavy-weight manual reviews for every entry. This document provides an operational decision matrix, sample metadata fields, required automated checks, rollout steps, and acceptance criteria for the intake flow. Links: PRD draft: drive.redwood/internal/prd/model-onboard/soft-pin-exemptions (placeholder), intake checklist spreadsheet: drive.redwood/internal/worksheets/model-intake.csv, runtime sanity tests repo: github.com/redwood/runtime/sanity-tests (PR link to be added in comments).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entries must declare a compatibility_profile field from the allowed set: [stable, variant-compatible, behavioral-sensitive]
Models tagged behavioral-sensitive are automatically marked as 'pin recommended' in the intake UI and require a manual sign-off to allow soft-pin
Runtime must expose two gating signals to the control plane: kv_format_compat and tokenizer_compat; both must be true for automatic soft-pin fallback to occur

Intake automation will run the runtime sanity test suite (subset) against the submitted weights; results recorded in the intake ticket and must pass >= 90% of established unit/acceptance checks for auto-approval
A documented fallback playbook exists (playbook link in comments) — including steps to pin traffic, invalidate caches, and an automated alert to customers and SRE when fallback triggers

Onboarding UI surfaces a clear reason when soft-pin is suppressed and provides the exact checks that failed (tokenizer mismatch, weight shape delta, KV cache checksum mismatch, runtime test fail), with links to artifacts
A one-click 'request exemption' workflow for licensing or regulatory reasons that attaches a mandatory justification field and assigns to Security and Catalog owners
Rollout validation: after an initial soft-pin rollout to 5% traffic for 48h without regression alerts, the model may be raised to general availability per rollout policy
scope: Introduce compatibility_profile metadata and validation rules in the intake form
Add runtime signals (kv_format_compat, tokenizer_compat) to the model metadata contract
Create automated sanity-test runner that returns pass/fail and a short failure taxonomy
Update console intake UX to show pin recommendation and exemption flow
Define playbook and alerting for soft-pin fallback operations
out_of_scope: Full overhaul of catalog data model or adding exhaustive provenance fields
Manual approval gates for all community models (we will only require manual sign-off for behavioral-sensitive or exempt cases)
Changes to billing model or pricing tiers
proposed_flow: 1) Author submits model via intake UI and selects license + expected compatibility_profile
2) Automated runner executes tokenizer_compat and KV/weight shape checks against a lightweight runtime shim
3) Runner invokes runtime sanity-test subset and produces a scored report (pass rate, failure taxonomy)
4) If compatibility_profile==stable and pass_rate>=90% and both signals true -> auto-approve with soft-pin enabled
5) If compatibility_profile==variant-compatible but any signal false or pass_rate<90% -> soft-pin suppressed; intake ticket requires catalog owner review
6) If compatibility_profile==behavioral-sensitive -> recommend pin; require manual sign-off to enable soft-pin; record rationale
7) Requests for exemptions (legal/regulatory) create a linked security review ticket and block auto-approval until resolved
decision_matrix: Row: profile=stable; kv=true; tokenizer=true; pass>=90% => Action: Auto-approve; soft-pin allowed
Row: profile=stable; any false or pass<90% => Action: Require manual review; soft-pin suppressed until remediation
Row: profile=variant-compatible; all true; pass>=95% => Action: Auto-approve; soft-pin allowed with 5% canary rollout
Row: profile=variant-compatible; mismatch in tokenizer or KV => Action: Soft-pin suppressed; suggest tokenizers/adapter layer work
Row: profile=behavioral-sensitive; any signals => Action: Pin recommended; must set strict_version=true unless explicit manual override with documented tests
dependencies: runtime: expose kv_format_compat and tokenizer_compat flags in model metadata API
engineering: lightweight runtime shim for running core sanity-tests in CI
console: intake UI update to show pin recommendation and exemption flow
security: review service for regulatory exemption requests
catalog team: update onboarding docs and acceptance checklists
risks: False negatives from the sanity-test suite could allow incompatible variants to be soft-pinned leading to production regressions
Overly strict defaults may increase manual review load and slow community model onboarding
Disagreements on classification (behavioral-sensitive vs variant-compatible) may cause categorical drift without clear arbitration
Runtime engineers will need to maintain the shim and tests as new model families arrive — potential maintenance burden
open_questions: What is the canonical list of checks included in the 'sanity-test subset' (tokenization, shape, basic LLM outputs)? Need runtime and research input
Can we reuse existing eval harnesses from the research team or must the runtime author bespoke micro-tests?
Should we permit a 'grace period' where a model is soft-pinned but monitored at 1% traffic for 7 days before raising to 5%?
What SLAs do we require for the automated runner (latency for intake validation) to keep the intake flow fast for engineers?
